title: Global ThemeProvider sync + opaque Ritual History dialog

requirements.summary: Add a single global ThemeProvider/ThemeContext that owns theme state, derives effectiveTheme, and is the only place that mutates the root DOM theme class.
acceptanceCriteria: Theme state has one source of truth via a React context provider.
`document.documentElement.classList` is only mutated inside the ThemeProvider (not scattered across multiple hooks/components).
The provider exposes both `theme` and `effectiveTheme` to consumers.

file_operations.description: Create a ThemeContext + ThemeProvider that stores `theme` ('light'|'dark'|'system') and derived `effectiveTheme` ('light'|'dark'), and centralizes applying/removing `light`/`dark` classes on `document.documentElement` in exactly one effect within the provider.

Wrap the authenticated app shell (and unauthenticated/login screens) with the new ThemeProvider so the entire app reads theme state from a single global source of truth without changing frontend/src/main.tsx.

requirements.summary: Refactor the theme hook API to consume ThemeContext, avoid DOM reads during render, and ensure only one system preference listener runs only when theme is 'system'.
acceptanceCriteria: ThemeToggle (and any other consumer) does not read `document.documentElement.classList` during render.
When `theme !== 'system'`, there is no active `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` change listener.
Switching OS light/dark while `theme === 'system'` updates `effectiveTheme` and the UI reactively without requiring a refresh.

file_operations.description: Refactor `useTheme` to become a lightweight consumer of the new ThemeContext (returning `theme`, `effectiveTheme`, and actions) with no DOM reads during render and no `matchMedia` listener creation here.

Add/organize an internal `useSystemThemeWatcher` (or equivalent provider-scoped logic) that installs exactly one `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` listener only while `theme === 'system'`, updating `effectiveTheme` reactively.

requirements.summary: Update ThemeToggle to render and toggle using ThemeContext values to eliminate icon/aria-label desynchronization.
acceptanceCriteria: ThemeToggle icon and aria-label always match the currently applied theme (`effectiveTheme`).
Toggling the theme updates the UI immediately and correctly without needing a rerender triggered by unrelated state.

file_operations.description: Update ThemeToggle to use `theme`/`effectiveTheme` and actions from the refactored `useTheme` (context-based) for icon state and aria-label, removing any render-time reads of `document.documentElement.classList`.

requirements.summary: Ensure theme persistence writes to localStorage only occur in explicit theme actions (set/toggle), not in effects or repeated renders.
acceptanceCriteria: LocalStorage key `theme` is written only when the user changes theme (set/toggle).
Reloading the app restores the saved theme preference and applies it correctly.

file_operations.description: Implement theme initialization by reading localStorage once (lazy init) and ensure localStorage writes for key `theme` happen only inside explicit theme action functions (e.g., `setTheme`/`toggleTheme`), not in effects tied to render cycles.
Ensure the hook API does not introduce any additional localStorage write paths (it should delegate persistence solely to ThemeProvider actions).

requirements.summary: Make the Home Ritual History entry dialog content fully opaque in light/dark themes via className overrides at the call site (no edits under components/ui).
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a Ritual History entry on the Home page shows an opaque dialog surface (text is clearly legible) in light mode.
Opening a Ritual History entry on the Home page shows an opaque dialog surface (text is clearly legible) in dark mode.
No changes are made to any files under `frontend/src/components/ui`.

file_operations.description: Update the Ritual History entry <DialogContent> call-site className to force a fully opaque surface (e.g., using an opaque background and appropriate border/shadow classes) for both light and dark themes, without modifying any files under frontend/src/components/ui.
